title: Effect of calcination time on the NH 3 -SCR performance of 8Fe 2 O 3 –5CeO 2 –40MnO 2 /TiO 2  catalysts
content: Low-temperature NH3-SCR catalysts can reduce the energy demand associated with reheating flue gas after desulfurization and particulate removal. In this work, 8Fe2O3–5CeO2–40MnO2/TiO2 catalysts were prepared by co-precipitation and calcined at 400 °C for different dwell times. Shorter treatment left the pore network and exposure of the active components insufficiently developed, whereas further extension of the dwell time provided an additional improvement in catalytic performance. However, extending the dwell time to 5 h provided no further catalytic benefit and was accompanied by renewed aggregation. Calcination for 4 h gave the best overall NH3-SCR response: NO conversion exceeded 80% from 115 to 425 °C and 90% from 129 to 390 °C, with a maximum of (99.17 ± 0.6)%, while N2 selectivity remained close to 100% below 225 °C. At 200 °C, the sample retained stabilized NO conversions of (84.8 ± 0.7)% under 60 ppm SO2 and (81.6 ± 0.8)% under 60 ppm SO2 and 5 vol% H2O. The structural and surface analyses showed well-developed porosity, weaker aggregation, greater exposure of the active components, increased surface acidity and improved reducibility after 4 h. This catalyst also exhibited the lowest apparent activation energy of 55.78 kJ mol−1. Under the conditions examined, calcination at 400 °C for 4 h provided the most suitable balance between physicochemical properties and catalytic performance.
